name: MEDIAN
description: MEDIAN returns the middle value of a set of numbers: the value with an equal number of values above and below it after sorting.
tldr: Finds the central (50th percentile) value of a dataset.

parameters.name: number1
parameters.description: The first number, cell, or range to evaluate.

parameters.name: number2
parameters.description: Additional numbers, cells, or ranges (optional). Up to 255 arguments.

basicExample.explanation: With 5 values the sorted middle (3rd) value is 3.

advancedExamples.title: Even number of values averages the two middle numbers
advancedExamples.description: When the count is even, MEDIAN averages the two central values.
advancedExamples.explanation: The two middle values are 2 and 3; (2+3)/2 = 2.5.

advancedExamples.title: Median ignores blanks and text automatically
advancedExamples.scenario: Mixed column with a repeated figure
advancedExamples.description: MEDIAN on a range with a duplicated central value.
advancedExamples.explanation: Sorted, the 3rd (middle) value is 20, so the median is 20.

howItWorks: MEDIAN sorts the numeric values it receives and returns the value at the center position. With an odd count it returns the single middle value; with an even count it returns the arithmetic mean of the two middle values. Text, logical values, and empty cells are ignored.

howToSteps.name: Select the result cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell where you want the median.

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =MEDIAN(range) using the cells to evaluate.

limitations: Ignores text, logical values, and empty cells, which can change the perceived count.
For an even number of values it returns an average, not one of the actual data points.
Cells with text-formatted numbers are treated as text and ignored.

commonErrors.cause: No numeric values were supplied to the function.
commonErrors.fix: Make sure the range or arguments contain at least one number.

commonErrors.cause: Numbers stored as text are ignored, shrinking the dataset.
commonErrors.fix: Convert text to numbers or use VALUE() before MEDIAN.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: MEDIAN works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: How does MEDIAN differ from AVERAGE?
faq.answer: MEDIAN is the middle value and is resistant to outliers; AVERAGE is the sum divided by count and is pulled by extreme values.

faq.question: Does MEDIAN include zero?
faq.answer: Yes, zero is a real numeric value and is counted in the ordering.

faq.question: What does MEDIAN return for an empty range?
faq.answer: It returns #NUM! because there is no numeric value to evaluate.
